finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the unauthenticated q query parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL statement with no parameter binding, allowing UNION-based reads of any table in shop.db.
finding.source: app.py:11 - request.args.get("q", ""), supplied by any unauthenticated HTTP client.
finding.sink: app.py:12 - db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'").fetchall(), results returned via jsonify at app.py:13.

trace.note: term taken raw from query string
term spliced into SQL text inside single-quoted literal
fetchall executes injected SQL; sqlite3 execute rejects stacked statements but allows UNION SELECT
injected rows returned to attacker in JSON

finding.guards_checked: No validation/escaping of term; no bound parameters on this query (contrast app.py:18 and app.py:25); sqlite3 single-statement restriction limits to reads/expressions but does not prevent injection; no authentication or authorization on the route.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:11 takes q raw from the query string, and app.py:12 splices it into the SQL f-string with no escaping, allowlist, or bound parameter. The /search route (app.py:9-10) has no authentication or authorization decorator. The parameterized queries at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do not apply to this route.
verdict.reason: An anonymous client can send q with a single quote and UNION SELECT to /search, and app.py:12 executes that text unparameterized, with the rows returned by jsonify at app.py:13; the only sqlite3 restriction (one statement per execute) does not stop UNION-based reads.

finding.claim: Possible unauthorized enumeration of product listings by owner: /by-owner returns id and name for any owner value supplied in the query string with no caller identity or ownership check. Low confidence; depends on whether owner listings are meant to be public.
finding.source: app.py:24 - request.args.get("owner", ""), supplied by any unauthenticated HTTP client.
finding.sink: app.py:25-26 - parameterized SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE owner = ?, returned via jsonify.
finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query (no SQLi); no authentication or ownership check; only id and name returned, not price.

verdict.guard_found: none. The owner value is read from the query string at app.py:24 and bound as a parameter at app.py:25 (no SQL injection). No authentication decorator, session check, or ownership check exists on the route (app.py:22-26), and the app has no auth anywhere. Response is id and name only (app.py:26).
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.py:24-26: any anonymous client can pass owner=... and receive id and name rows, and no control between app.py:24 and app.py:26 blocks it. Severity is low, though, because the same app exposes id and name for every product to anonymous callers via /search (app.py:11-13), so the only new information is the owner-to-product mapping, and whether that counts as a vulnerability depends on an intent question the code cannot answer.
